newsitem.title: FRANCE: Daewoo head slams Europe on jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo head slams Europe on jobs - paper.

text.p: Daewoo Electronics chairman Soon-Hoon Bae, in an interview published on Tuesday, accused Europe of pursuing policies that discouraged foreign investment and jobs.
"I am not here to create social security but to create jobs and make profits," he told the International Herald Tribune in an interview conducted at Daewoo's Paris headquarters.

Bae renewed criticism of France's independent privatisation commission for blocking Daewoo from acquiring Thomson Multimedia (TMM) as part of a deal in which Lagardere Group had hoped to acquire the rest of the state-owned Thomson SA group.

But he reserved his harshest words for European leaders like Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene who have threatened legal action against French automaker Renault for deciding to close down a plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium, employing 3,100 people.
"This is not a legal issue," he said. "They should think about how to sell more cars. You cannot maintain state-subsidised make-work jobs."

"If you want to create jobs, then the state should create the right business environment, and that means investing in infrastructure, providing tax incentives for companies and training for workers, and offering hospitality to foreign managers."

Bae said Daewoo was still ready to examine a proposal to acquire Thomson Multimedia but rejected ideas he attributed to "the French press" that his group should either buy an initial minority stake in Thomson or join a consortium of several companies.
"My message is that I am waiting, and depending on the procedure that is decided for the Thomson privatisation I will come up with a proposal to create jobs."
In the meantime, he said, Daewoo is going ahead with plans to invest 1.7 billion francs in a new factory in France to make glass for televisions and computers.
While many in France view Thomson Multimedia as Thomson SA's crown jewel, "it's really more of a big headache," he said.

"I don't need the Thomson technology and I don't need the brand...They think I'm hiding something, but all I am proposing is to increase my manufacturing capacity in Europe and instead of setting up a new plant, I want to use an existing plant."
